Processed food apparently induces continuous insulin production in the human body, possibly due not only to large amounts of highly glycemic ingredients but also to the resulting diet composition, in terms of macronutrients, from consuming these products [ 76 , 83 , 106 – 108 ].

A detrimental diet composition may produce a hormonal imbalance that could turn into a negative loop where individuals accumulate fat, but are not properly nourished which makes them constantly hungry, causing them to eat more from that diet composition.

We propose to revise the current concept of causes for obesity. Instead of placing prime importance on the energy balance, i.e. concept 1, we suggest to emphasize the effect of food on the metabolism. The guiding principle should be: ‘Overweight and obesity are determined by a hormonal imbalance characterized by a constant and sustained secretion of insulin, which results from particular dietary compositions. These are closely linked to modern food habits.’

If the body constantly stores fat but does not use it as a source for energy, it would not only grow bigger but also become constantly hungry. This would possibly cause a repeated intake of the diet that is at the origin of the imbalance, thus making the body even bigger and hungrier and so on.
That means that when insulin is high due to food intake, the breakdown of fat from adipose tissue stops and fat storage starts [ 73 , 81 ].
